title: Hierarchy of discriminative power and complexity in learning quantum ensembles: sufficiency of $k=N$ for full discriminative power (Theorem A.3)
author: Jian Yao, Pengtao Li, Xiaohui Chen, Quntao Zhuang
work: Hierarchy of discriminative power and complexity in learning quantum ensembles
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem A.3 (source0.tex lines 973--990, source label thm: k=N full discriminative power), 'Sufficiency: k=N gives full discriminative power for ensembles with at most N pure states' - if the N-th moment operators of two ensembles of at most N distinct pure states agree, the ensembles coincide up to permutation - delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 992--1113 (122 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is the sufficiency half of the paper's central hierarchy statement: it shows that N SWAP-test moments already determine an N-state ensemble, so the MMD-k hierarchy reaches full discriminative power exactly at k=N. The proof is a substantial research-level argument, not a citation: it first propagates the equality M_N(E_1)=M_N(E_2) downwards to all moments M_t with 1<=t<=N through the article's hierarchy lemma, then converts equal moment operators into equal expectations of every homogeneous polynomial of degree t by the symmetric-tensor representation, then extracts the individual ensemble weights by exhibiting, for each index i, a separating linear functional from the hyperplane-separation lemma and applying the polynomial-moment identity to the rank-one test function built from it, and finally concludes p_i=q_i for every i. That sequence (moment hierarchy, symmetric-tensor representation of homogeneous polynomials, hyperplane separation, and the induced weight recovery) is a genuine multi-step construction. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem with a fully written proof of moderate length whose individual steps are non-trivial and whose conclusion is a new structural result.
